test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Matric Level) - Quant (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A tangent XY at point X of a circle with radius 7 cm meets a line through the center O at point Y such that OY = 25 cm. What is the length of the tangent XY?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, forming a right-angled triangle.

In ΔOXY, OX = 7 cm (radius) and OY = 25 cm (hypotenuse).

Using the **Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25)**:

XY² = 25² − 7² = 625 − 49 = 576.

XY = √576 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OX) = 7 cm

Distance from center O to point Y (OY) = 25 cm

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67bb9e8d51c42fe9edc7a9bae17f7981142d7c0cbd9c8f17f960dd1465396fd8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In a circle, the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact.

⇒ ∠OXY = 90°

⇒ In right-angled ΔOXY, using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ OY² = OX² + XY²

⇒ 25² = 7² + XY²

⇒ 625 = 49 + XY²

⇒ XY² = 625 − 49

⇒ XY² = 576

⇒ XY = √576

⇒ XY = 24 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

**__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. This always creates a right-angled triangle between the center, the point of contact, and any point on the tangent.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets used in competitive exams include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), and (20, 21, 29).

Tangents from External Point

The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal. Also, the line joining the external point to the center bisects the angle between the two tangents.</p
